sources.verifiedClaim: JCS preserves array order and Unicode strings, rejects duplicate names and lone surrogates, uses UTF-16 property-name ordering and ECMAScript number serialization. It is not an Internet Standards Track specification.
sources.decision: Do not equate generic Python sort_keys serialization with JCS. D1 makes only a bounded Python byte-contract claim; JCS adoption would require implementation and cross-runtime vectors.

sources.verifiedClaim: This specific draft permits documented time-based key expiry/purge and suggests HTTP 422 on changed payload under an existing key.
sources.decision: Historical work in progress, not a current standard or mandatory HTTP mapping. No claim that revision 07 is the latest revision. The first local adapter is not an HTTP service.

readSections: Ensuring Idempotency; idempotent create APIs with a client token
sources.classification: AWS SDK for .NET V3 vendor documentation
sources.verifiedClaim: For its listed token-based create operations, Proton documents eight-hour token expiry and possible new resource creation on retry after expiry. The listed operations are CreateEnvironmentTemplateVersion, CreateServiceTemplateVersion and CreateEnvironmentAccountConnection.
sources.decision: A scoped vendor counterexample to universal permanent deduplication. Do not generalize the rule to every Proton operation or to all services. CreateService uses a different documented idempotency group.
